items.title: Apple’s noise-canceling AirPods 4 are down to one of their best prices to date
items.raw:
The latest AirPods 4 offer good noise cancellation for their price, tuning out distracting noises well enough when you’re listening to music.	

The AirPods Pro 3 may be on sale for $199 ($50 off), but that’s still a lot of money. If you want noise cancellation for less, fortunately you can buy the AirPods 4 with Active Noise Cancellation for $119 ($60 off) at Amazon and Walmart. That’s the cheapest they’ve been since the holidays, and only $20 more than their lowest price to date.
Apple Airpods 4 with ANC

Where to Buy:

 $179 $119 at Amazon
 $179 $119 at Walmart

For the price, the AirPods 4 do a surprisingly good job of tuning out the outside world. While they don’t drown out noise as completely as the AirPods Pro, they significantly reduce ambient and low-frequency sounds on planes and in offices, especially when listening to music. In our testing, outside noise was easy to ignore even with the volume set to about 50 percent.
Beyond noise cancellation, the AirPods 4 offer the best sound we’ve heard from an entry-level AirPods model so far, with richer bass than previous generations. They also add a more robust IP54 rating for water and dust resistance and even boast a few Pro-level features, including wireless charging support, a built-in speaker on the charging case so you can track them via Apple’s Find My app, and crystal clear call quality. You also get other perks like support for live translation courtesy of an iOS 26 update, along with a natural-sounding transparency mode.
That said, they’re still the more affordable model, so you miss out on extras like a heart rate sensor, on-ear volume controls, and the ability to use them as hearing aids. Still, they deliver most of what people actually want at a much lower price.
Read our AirPods 4 review.

items.title: The arts of war: can Europe’s artists embrace the idea of ‘armed pacifism’?

• Don’t get This Is Europe delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
One reason why art – painting, literature, film, theatre, all of it – is so important to society is that it creates spaces that can tolerate difficult answers to difficult questions. This makes art the opposite of politics, where politicians are under constant pressure to give easy answers to difficult questions.
I was thinking about this distinction this month while watching the European film awards, this continent’s answer to the Oscars, which has moved its annual ceremony to January this year as it seeks to position itself as a major tastemaker for grownup cinema.

items.title: ‘Air conditioners are struggling’: parts of NSW, Queensland and Victoria swelter as heat records tumble
items.raw:
Bushfires still burning out of control in Victoria as temperatures reached the high 40s in the west of NSW 

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

People across significant parts of western New South Wales, south-western Queensland, Victoria and the ACT have suffered through another day of sweltering conditions, with more local records tumbling around the country and temperatures in some alpine areas exceeding 30C for the first time.
Temperatures reached the high 40s again in the west of NSW, climbing to 49.2C at Borrona Downs in the far west. All-time heat records were set at Tibooburra (48.7C), Hay Airport in south-western NSW (48.4C) and White Cliffs, which at 48.3C broke the record of 48.2C set the previous day. Yarrawonga in north-east Victoria had its hottest day, reaching 46C.
